title: Pinned version tolerance and semantic regression spec
creator: Anika Shah
description:
Goal: define a compact, machine- and human-readable contract that governs what we guarantee for a pinned model version and the published performance profile. The contract covers three domains: 1) semantic/io compatibility (prompt shape, accepted parameter aliases, response structure), 2) behavioral tolerance (semantic fingerprint deltas, confidence/score drift thresholds), and 3) performance & resource profile (throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency for canonical sequence-length buckets, expected memory/KV cache characteristics, and quantization compatibility).

Scope and deliverables:
- A contract document template and a JSON schema for the published 'pinned-version-profile' artifact that lives in the model onboarding registry. The schema includes: model_id, pinned_version, io_schema, alias_map, output_shape_signature, semantic_fingerprint_sample_ids, semantic_tolerance_bands, perf_profile (seq_buckets, batch_sizes, p50/p95/p99, tokens_per_sec), mem_profile, quantization_compat (supported qbits and expected perf delta), rollback_triggers, and gated_tests.
- Acceptance criteria and gating tests that run in CI and on the onboarding pipeline: unit-level io-conformance tests, a semantic-regression evaluation suite (sampled prompts + fingerprint comparison), and performance snapshot checks against the declared perf_profile.
- A published artifact format: JSON-LD for machine discoverability + a human-readable Confluence summary. We will also publish a CSV perf matrix for quick ingestion by cost/console tooling.
- Operational controls: definition of allowed parameter aliases (e.g., 'temperature' vs 'temp'), explicit mapping rules, and alias deprecation policy with a 2-cycle compatibility window.
- Degradation policy: numeric tolerance bands (epsilon values) for token-level probability drift, output shape soft-failing rules (e.g., optional fields can be missing up to N% of samples), and a rollback policy triggered by cross-customer regression detection or perf regression above defined thresholds.

Design decisions and trade-offs made so far:
- Use semantic fingerprinting (embedding-based median distance + categorical token distribution deltas) as the primary behavioral signal rather than only surface-level token edit distance. This balances sensitivity to meaningful change with robustness to innocuous surface variations.
- We will allow conservative aliasing for parameters to ease SDK migration, but aliased names must be listed in alias_map in the published profile. Aliases will be accepted at runtime and normalized; SDKs will warn on deprecated aliases after the compatibility window.
- Tolerance bands are asymmetric: we penalize regressions (worse quality/latency) more aggressively than improvements. This minimizes surprise for customers who pin versions to avoid regressions.

Acceptance criteria (must be `pass` to mark onboarding Done):
1) IO conformance: 100% of canonical prompt shapes accepted; output_shape_signature verified against sample set.
2) Semantic regression: median embedding distance delta <= 0.035 for the model's canonical eval set; max categorical label drift <= 3% for classification tasks.
3) Performance: p95 latency for seq-length 256 with batch=1 must be within the declared perf_profile +/- 10%; throughput for production batching modes should not regress more than 15% from profile.
4) Documentation: JSON-LD artifact published to the onboarding registry, Confluence page authored, and perf CSV uploaded to S3 for console consumption.

Testing artifacts and links:
- Regression harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/regression-harness (CI job: `onboard:pinned-checks`)
- Draft JSON schema: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/MI/Pinned+Version+Profile+Schema
- Example onboarding PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/678 (contains sample perf CSV and fingerprint vectors)
- Runtime integration PR (blocks release until passing): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345

Next steps / rollout plan:
- Merge JSON schema into onboarding registry (ENG-43910 dependency) and wire CI gating into onboarding pipeline (owner: Marco Li).
- Run pilot onboarding for two internal models and publish profiles; gather feedback from SDK/console teams for alias handling and perf matrix ingestion.
- Instrument user-facing console to surface 'pinned-profile mismatch' alerts when deployed model behavior drifts past tolerances.

Notes on publication format and discoverability:
- JSON-LD keys must include a `contract_version` and `signed_by` (onboarding owner). The console reads the perf CSV and JSON-LD; cost tooling consumes tokens_per_sec and p95 values to compute projected unit costs.

Operational playbook snippet (extracted):
- If semantic regression is detected (CI or production): triage -> snapshot failing prompts -> determine rollback vs remediate -> notify customers with a pinned-version advisory.
- For alias deprecations: deprecate in alias_map, emit SDK warnings for two release cycles, then remove alias from runtime acceptance list.

This ticket is the canonical spec; follow-ups will create implementation tickets for schema validation, CI gating, console ingestion, and customer advisory automation.
